title: Dimension difference on minimal components of a flat local map
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ and $(B,\mathfrak n,L)$ be nonzero commutative local $k$-algebras essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], and let $f:A\to B$ be a flat local $k$-algebra homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], where local means $f^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak m$, $K=A/\mathfrak m$, and $L=B/\mathfrak n$. A prime is minimal when it contains no strictly smaller prime. Contraction gives a surjection from the set of minimal primes of $B$ onto that of $A$. For every minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ and $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ set $E=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$ and $H=\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)$, with the inclusion induced by $f$. All dimensions and transcendence degrees below are finite nonnegative integers [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring, def-kun-transcendence-degree], and
$$\dim(A/\mathfrak p)+\operatorname{trdeg}_k K=\operatorname{trdeg}_k E,\qquad
\dim(B/\mathfrak q)+\operatorname{trdeg}_k L=\operatorname{trdeg}_k H.$$
For the induced field map $K\to L$ one has the integer identity
$$\dim(B/\mathfrak q)-\dim(A/\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{trdeg}_E H-\operatorname{trdeg}_K L.$$
Surjectivity of contraction asserts existence of a minimal prime over every minimal prime downstairs; it does not assert uniqueness, a bijection, or flatness of $A/\mathfrak p\to B/\mathfrak q$. No smoothness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q$ be a minimal prime of $B$ and put $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Contraction preserves primality: if $ab\in\mathfrak p$, then $f(a)f(b)\in\mathfrak q$, so one factor belongs to $\mathfrak q$. For any prime $\mathfrak p_0\subseteq\mathfrak p$, flat going down gives a prime $\mathfrak q_0\subseteq\mathfrak q$ contracting to $\mathfrak p_0$. Minimality of $\mathfrak q$ forces $\mathfrak q_0=\mathfrak q$, whence $\mathfrak p_0=\mathfrak p$. Thus contraction sends minimal primes to minimal primes.

source.place: Tag 00HS (lemma-flat-going-down), applied below a minimal prime

proof.text: The map $f$ is flat and local, so the faithful-flatness node gives surjectivity on spectra. Given a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, choose a prime $Q$ of $B$ over it. The prime-containment node, with $I=0$, gives a minimal prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq Q$. Its contraction is a prime contained in $\mathfrak p$, hence is $\mathfrak p$ by minimality. This proves surjectivity on minimal primes without a uniqueness assertion.

For the dimension calculation, take either $(D,\mathfrak d,\mathfrak a)=(A,\mathfrak m,\mathfrak p)$ or $(B,\mathfrak n,\mathfrak q)$. By essential finite type write $D=W^{-1}C$ as a $k$-algebra, with $C$ finite type over $k$. Put $\mathfrak r=\{c\in C:c/1\in\mathfrak d\}$. The localization-prime-residue-field node, part (2), identifies $C_{\mathfrak r}$ with $D_{\mathfrak d}$. Since $D$ is local, every denominator outside $\mathfrak d$ is a unit; $d/s\mapsto ds^{-1}$ is inverse to $D\to D_{\mathfrak d}$. Hence $D\simeq C_{\mathfrak r}$ over $k$. Under this isomorphism the maximal ideal is $\mathfrak rC_{\mathfrak r}$, as a fraction $c/s$ is a unit precisely when $c\notin\mathfrak r$.

Let $\mathfrak a_0$ be the contraction of $\mathfrak a$ to $C$. The same localization node, part (1), gives $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak a_0C_{\mathfrak r}$; also $\mathfrak a_0\subseteq\mathfrak r$. Put $T=C/\mathfrak a_0$ and $\mathfrak r_T=\mathfrak r/\mathfrak a_0$. The quotient-localization node gives $D/\mathfrak a\simeq T_{\mathfrak r_T}$ by $(c+\mathfrak a_0)/(s+\mathfrak a_0)\mapsto c/s+\mathfrak a$. Here $T$ is a nonzero domain, and the images of finitely many algebra generators of $C$ generate $T$, so it is finite type over $k$. Reducing this isomorphism modulo the maximal ideals gives $D/\mathfrak d\simeq\kappa_T(\mathfrak r_T)$. The map $T\to T_{\mathfrak r_T}$ is injective, since a zero fraction $t/1$ implies $st=0$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak r_T$, and $T$ is a domain. Every target element is $t/s$ with $s/1$ a unit; the unit-denominator fraction-equivalence node therefore identifies $\operatorname{Frac}(T)$ with $\operatorname{Frac}(D/\mathfrak a)$ over $k$.

source.place: Tags 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization) and 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient); fraction-field comparison by the cited unit-denominator lemma

proof.text: Apply the dimension-at-point-components node to the finite type domain $T$ at $\mathfrak r_T$. Its unique minimal prime is $(0)$, contained in $\mathfrak r_T$, so $\dim_{\mathfrak r_T}\operatorname{Spec}T=\dim T$. The finite-type-domain node gives $\dim T=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\operatorname{Frac}(T)$, finite. The local-ring dimension node gives, with finite terms, $\dim_{\mathfrak r_T}\operatorname{Spec}T=\dim T_{\mathfrak r_T}+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_T(\mathfrak r_T)$. Substituting the explicit identifications from the preceding step yields $\dim(D/\mathfrak a)+\operatorname{trdeg}_k(D/\mathfrak d)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\operatorname{Frac}(D/\mathfrak a)$; these are nonnegative finite integers. A ring isomorphism preserves prime chains, hence dimension; a field isomorphism over $k$ preserves algebraic independence and transcendence bases, hence transcendence degree. Taking both choices of $D$ proves the two asserted formulas and the finiteness of their terms.

The map $A/\mathfrak p\to B/\mathfrak q$ is injective because $f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$, and extends to $E\to H$ by $a/b\mapsto f(a)/f(b)$. Locality similarly makes $A/\mathfrak m\to B/\mathfrak n$, namely $K\to L$, injective. Both maps respect $k$. Apply the tower node to $k\to E\to H$ and $k\to K\to L$: $\operatorname{trdeg}_k H=\operatorname{trdeg}_E H+\operatorname{trdeg}_k E$ and $\operatorname{trdeg}_k L=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L+\operatorname{trdeg}_k K$. Since their left sides are finite by step 5, both relative degrees are finite as well, and cardinal addition is ordinary addition here. Subtracting the two dimension formulas of step 5 in $\mathbf Z$ gives $\dim(B/\mathfrak q)-\dim(A/\mathfrak p)=(\operatorname{trdeg}_k H-\operatorname{trdeg}_k E)-(\operatorname{trdeg}_k L-\operatorname{trdeg}_k K)=\operatorname{trdeg}_E H-\operatorname{trdeg}_K L$. This uses neither smoothness nor flatness of the component quotient map.
